text:
Predicates:
CanRegisterVote(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
ParticipateElection(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 U.S. presidential election.
CitizenshipUS(x) ::: x has United States citizenship.
CitizenshipTWN(x) ::: x has Taiwanese citizenship.
OfficialRF(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
ManagerAtGazprom(x) ::: x is a manager at Gazprom.
HoldCitizenship(x, y) ::: x holds citizenship y.
NepCitizenship(x, y) ::: x does not hold citizenship y.
---

Premises:
∀x (CanRegisterVote(x) → ParticipateElection(x)) ::: Everyone who can register to vote in the U.S. can participate in the election.
CitizenshipUS(x) → CanRegisterVote(x) ::: If someone has U.S. citizenship, then they can register to vote in the U.S.
CitizenshipUS(x) ∨ CitizenshipTWN(x) ::: A person either has U.S. or Taiwanese citizenship.
¬HoldCitizenship(vladimir, Taiwanese) ::: Vladimir does not hold Taiwanese citizenship.
¬(HoldCitizenship(vladimir, Taiwanese) ∨ ManagerAtGazprom(vladimir)) ::: Vladimir neither holds Taiwanese citizenship nor is he a manager at Gazprom.
---

Conclusion:
CanRegisterVote(ekaterina) ∨ ManagerAtGazprom(ekaterina) ::: Ekaterina can participate in the 2024 U.S. presidential election or is a manager at Gazprom.
